outcome.answer: The papers cover low-precision training and distributed learning, but not a single approach combining low precision, distributed training, and private devices. For large-model training, FP4 methods aim to improve efficiency while preserving accuracy: studies examine stable FP4 recipes and scaling, and adaptive block scaling to reduce quantization error [1, 2, 3]. AGoQ quantizes activations and gradients to reduce memory and communication time in multi-GPU LLM training [7]. For distributed reinforcement-learning post-training, PULSE reduces communication by sending only updates that affect low-precision forward passes [4]. For privacy, a separate study speeds differentially private fine-tuning through low-rank gradient methods, but does not address low-precision arithmetic or distributed devices [6]. RockNet trains across ultra-low-power devices, but its abstract does not describe low-precision numbers or privacy guarantees [8].
